instructions: Cut 2 or 3 slashes into each of the chicken thighs. Grate the ginger and mince the 6 garlic cloves. Finely chop the 2 onions and the 3 tomatoes.

In a large bowl, mix the ginger, garlic, the juice of half the lemon, 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp Kashmiri chili powder and 3/4 tsp of the salt. Add the chicken and rub it into the cuts. Leave it while you make the masala.

Put the 3 dried red chilies, the cinnamon stick, 5 cloves, star anise, 6 cardamom pods, 1 tsp peppercorns, 1 1/2 tsp fennel seeds, 1 tsp cumin seeds and 1 1/2 tbsp coriander seeds in a dry skillet over medium low. Stir them constantly for 6 to 8 minutes, until the coriander turns golden and crunchy and the kitchen smells toasty. Don't let them go dark. Transfer them onto a plate to cool.
In the same pan, warm 1/2 tbsp of the oil over medium low. Add the 1/3 cup coconut and the leaves from 1 sprig of curry leaves and stir for 4 to 5 minutes, until the coconut is light golden.
Grind the cooled spices to a fine powder in a spice grinder or blender. Add the coconut and curry leaves, the 10 cashews and 1/2 cup cold water and blend to a smooth paste.
Heat the remaining 2 1/2 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium. Add the bay leaf and the onions and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until they're light golden. Don't rush the onions.
Turn the heat to high, add the chicken with everything in the bowl and cook for 5 minutes, turning the pieces, until the outside turns opaque and browns in places.
Add the tomatoes and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Cook over medium for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes collapse and you can see oil shining at the edges.
Stir in the leaves from the other 2 curry leaf sprigs, then the masala paste and 1 cup hot water. Scrape up anything stuck to the bottom of the pot.

Bring it to a simmer, cover and cook over low for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the chicken is tender. You're cooking it to 175°F at the thickest part, so if you have a thermometer, check it there, away from the bone. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece next to the bone: it's done when the juices run clear and there's no pink.
If the gravy is thin, boil it uncovered over medium high for a few minutes, until it coats the chicken. If it's too thick, stir in a splash of hot water.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the other half of the lemon.
Serve with steamed rice or chapati.
method_notes: All three dry roast a Chettinad blend of dried red chilies, black pepper, fennel, cumin, coriander and whole sweet spices, grind it to a paste and cook it into a base of onions and tomatoes with bone-in chicken. Swasthi's marinates the chicken briefly with lemon, ginger, garlic and turmeric, roasts coconut with curry leaves and grinds it into the masala with cashews, then fries the chicken with the onions before the tomatoes and paste go in. Cooking and Me grinds a smaller blend with garlic and cashews, marinates the chicken in it with yogurt and finishes with cream and kasuri methi; Fun Food Frolic grinds ginger and garlic into the paste, skips the coconut and roasts the paste in the pot until deep brown before the chicken goes in. This one follows Swasthi's but leaves out the stone flower (kalpasi), which is hard to find outside Indian shops.
